query: For boride-based components used in hot-dip aluminum-plating equipment, what single intervention could improve resistance to molten-aluminum corrosion? Formulate one hypothesis that identifies the intervention, explains its mechanism, predicts the improvement relative to an appropriate baseline, defines the conditions under which it should remain effective, cites supporting prior evidence, and specifies a controlled experiment whose results could falsify the hypothesis.

generation.hypothesis: The addition of rare earth ions, specifically 1 wt% of Cerium (Ce), to boride-based components will improve their resistance to molten-aluminum corrosion by 35% relative to the baseline of untreated boride-based components, under the conditions of high temperature (700°C) and exposure to molten aluminum for 100 hours, through the mechanism of forming a protective oxide layer on the surface that hinders the diffusion of aluminum ions into the material.
generation.material_initial_state: Boride-based components in their as-fabricated state
generation.intervention: Addition of 1 wt% of Cerium (Ce) to the boride-based components
generation.conditions: High temperature (700°C) and exposure to molten aluminum for 100 hours
generation.structural_mediator: Protective oxide layer formed on the surface of the boride-based components
generation.mechanism: Hindrance of aluminum ion diffusion into the material through the protective oxide layer
generation.predicted_outcome: 35% improvement in resistance to molten-aluminum corrosion
generation.uncertainty: The actual improvement in corrosion resistance may vary depending on the specific composition of the boride-based components and the processing conditions. Further research is needed to optimize the amount of Cerium addition and the processing parameters.

falsification_experiment.design: Controlled experiment with treated and untreated boride-based components exposed to molten aluminum at 700°C for 100 hours
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the treated boride-based components show less than 20% improvement in corrosion resistance compared to the untreated components, the hypothesis is falsified.
